serp_review.query: why is gmail storage still full after deleting emails
serp_review.observation: The standard web search returned third-party blogs (picbackman, clean.email, multcloud, dev.to, a twit.tv post) and a forum thread. Most of them name Trash, the shared quota and an update delay. Some cite timing that doesn't match Google's (for example 'seven days'). They raise mail-client sync as a cause, but none of them cite Google's IMAP documentation. None of them give a symptom-to-check table or a size-versus-count check.
serp_review.limitation: One standard US web search. This is not a Google-specific ranking capture. Result pages were not opened individually.

information_gain: A symptom → cause → check → next-step table for 'I deleted and nothing changed'. It covers mail still in Trash or Spam, deletion in an IMAP client that leaves mail in All Mail (sourced to Google's IMAP settings page), Drive or Photos dominating, count versus size (larger:10M), the wrong account, and Google's stated 48–72 hour update window. A matching ordered checklist follows. Existing site pages state the Trash and 48–72 hour facts. None of them diagnose why the number didn't move after a deletion, and none cover the IMAP All Mail route.
overlap_check: Hub gmail-mailbox-full-cant-receive-emails covers delivery when full. how-to-free-up-gmail-storage and gmail-storage-upgrade-vs-cleanup cover how to reduce usage. gmail-empty-trash-automatically covers the 30-day rule. This draft links to them rather than repeating their recipes. The pending sibling gmail-empty-trash-storage-still-full (after emptying Trash) remains distinct. This draft stops at the decision to empty Trash and doesn't cover the post-emptying diagnostic tree. A reviewer should confirm the two don't converge.
limitations: Source and documentation review only. No live Gmail mailbox, IMAP client or storage-page test was run, and no screenshots exist.
IMAP behaviour depends on the client and on Gmail IMAP settings. The article uses hedged 'can' wording and doesn't verify specific clients.
The phone-app swipe default (archive versus delete) was not found in a Google source, so the article doesn't claim it.
Google's 48–72 hour figure is described as 'normally', not guaranteed. The article doesn't give a countdown.
Workspace pooled or admin-set quotas are not covered.
